# RAT-85 M4: after the target withdraws its environment support, the same
# pair still reaches the server, which replays it before planning. A new
# create is refused by the CLI's preflight, and an explicit new pair, which
# skips that preflight, is refused by the server.

env-domain D
skygo --token-file=$TOKEN_FILE env create -f web.yaml --request-id web-1 --request-domain $D
stdout ' web +modeled +present +creating '
env-id E web
env-reconcile

env-withdraw
skygo --token-file=$TOKEN_FILE env create -f web.yaml --request-id web-1 --request-domain $D
stderr '^request-domain: '$D'$'
stderr '^request-id: web-1$'
stdout '^'$E' +web +modeled +present +ready '

! skygo --token-file=$TOKEN_FILE env create -f db.yaml
stderr 'target "modeled" does not advertise persistent-environments-v1'
! stderr 'request-id:'
! skygo --token-file=$TOKEN_FILE env create -f db.yaml --request-id db-1 --request-domain $D
stderr 'invalid_argument: unsupported environment spec'
env-records after.txt
grep -count=1 'sessions=' after.txt

# The withdrawal survives a restart; so does the replay.
env-restart
skygo --token-file=$TOKEN_FILE env create -f web.yaml --request-id web-1 --request-domain $D
stdout '^'$E' +web '

-- web.yaml --
name: web
target: modeled
image: task:v1
cpu_millis: 100
memory_bytes: 1048576
-- db.yaml --
name: db
target: modeled
image: task:v1
cpu_millis: 100
memory_bytes: 1048576
